findings.summary: Z2 pins `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` without `-z`. By default git quotes paths that hold non-ASCII bytes, `"` or `\` (core.quotePath). A valid name such as `docs/es/guía.md` comes out as `"docs/es/gu\303\255a.md"`, which CheckFilePath rejects because of the `"` and `\`. The repository test would fail on a file the module zip accepts, and the rejected line would print git's quoted form instead of the path.
findings.evidence: git-config(1) core.quotePath; module.fileNameOK (golang.org/x/mod@v0.37.0/module/module.go:278-295) allows unicode letters but not `"` or `\`. The repository has no non-ASCII path today: `git ls-files | LC_ALL=C grep '[^A-Za-z0-9._/+~-]'` lists only the 11 `it's repo` paths. Its `es` language support makes accented names a realistic addition.
findings.fix: Write `git ls-files -z --cached --others --exclude-standard` (split on NUL) in Z2. Optionally add a planted case: an untracked `ñ.txt` produces no line.

findings.section: Executive summary (the goal); Why this shape (fix forward, retract rc.2)
findings.summary: UNSURE. The claim that the retraction 'takes effect once v0.15.0 is out' holds only if v0.15.0 becomes Go's 'latest', the highest release the proxy lists, retractions ignored. go.mod says the v1.0.0 tag was removed, but the module proxy usually keeps versions it has served. If the proxy still lists v1.0.0, Go reads retractions from v1.0.0's go.mod. Then neither `retract v1.0.0` nor the new `retract v0.15.0-rc.2` ever takes effect from a v0.x release.
findings.evidence: go.mod:16-18 (the v1.0.0 retraction and its comment). cmd/go modload queryLatestVersionIgnoringRetractions queries 'latest', which prefers the highest release. I could not list the module's versions in this session: reading the module cache and `git tag` were denied.
findings.fix: Settle it with `go list -m github.com/mvelosop/vloop@latest`; v0.14.0 confirms the claim. If it shows v1.0.0, reword the summary and the 'Why' bullet: Z4 records the intent but takes effect only once a v1.0.x that retracts itself is published. Z4 itself does not change.

findings.summary: The repository's architect skill requires domain invariants to be cited by ID. The entry says only 'the invariants on the run's state; sessions never edit .vloop/'. The invariants that apply are S-4 (sessions write nothing under .vloop/ but .vloop/tmp/; the plan session writes the gate folders), S-2 (sessions never commit or move refs) and P-4 (gates are authored before the work, by the plan session). P-4 and S-4 are the ones behind the constraint that no gate fixture may hold a `'` path.
findings.fix: `docs/domain/domain-model.md` — S-2, S-4 and P-4: sessions never edit .vloop/ or move refs; gate folders are the plan session's, and no fixture there may hold a path the module zip rejects.

After this run the base is 56bf0155 or later, and none of those commits has report.py or hook.py. Z1 pins d7b9cbb5 but does not ask for the header to say so. An earlier draft of this brief made exactly that mistake.
findings.evidence: tools/copilot-acceptance/kit/testdata/gen.sh:5-7. `git ls-tree -r --name-only 56bf0155 | grep report.py` finds nothing. Running gen.sh with d7b9cbb5's report.py, hook.py and bypass.sh and HEAD's vloop gives `diff -r` against golden empty, exit 0 (checked in this review).
findings.fix: Add to Z1: gen.sh's header names d7b9cbb5 as the commit whose report.py, hook.py and bypass.sh it runs.
